Hi All
I would like to add a title to each of the resulting dataframes and then after applying rbind, have a column in the resulting combined file that identifies each so I can compare values.

This is what the code looks like right now. I need the next steps.

f <- c("NoChange_MINU", "T5only_MINU", "P2Only_MINU","t2p5_MINU")
s <- stack(f)
names(s) <- gsub('_MINU', '', f)
rcl <- matrix(c(0,0.2,1, 0.2, 0.4,2,.4,.6,3,.6,.8,4,.8,1,5), ncol=3, byrow=T)
r <- reclassify(s, rcl)
rl = list()
for (i in 1:nlayers(r)) { rl[[i]] = zonal(a, r[[i]], 'sum') }
rl

~~~~Results in this:
[[1]]

#COMPUTING THE POSTERIOR

p_CD_Rep<-sample.naive.posterior(CDRa4c, n=10000, nobs=nrow(CD_Rep))
colnames(p_CD_Rep)<-c("a", "q2mi", "s")

#PLOTTING
par(mfrow=c(1,1))
plot(AvgDens~Year, data=CD_Rep, type="n", xaxp=c(2010,2012,2), main="Clarkia Reproduction")

points(AvgDens~Year, data=CD_Rep_cg, col="grey10")

Tmin.seq<-seq(from=7.33, to=8.82, by=0.01)

mu.CG <- sapply( Tmin.seq , function(z)

mean(exp(p_CD_Rep$a+p_CD_Rep$q2mi*z+p_CD_Rep$s*0) ))

mu.ci.CP <- sapply( Tmin.seq , function(z)

PCI(exp(p_CD_Rep$a+p_CD_Rep$q2mi*z+p_CD_Rep$s*1) ))

#####  And below is where I'm having trouble

lines(Tmin.seq, mu.CG, lwd=3, col="grey10")
lines(Tmin.seq, mu.CP, lwd=3, col="grey60")
lines(Tmin.seq, mu.ci.CG <http://mu.ci.CG>[1,], lty=2, col="grey10")

lines(Tmin.seq, mu.ci.CP[1,], lty=2, col="grey60")
lines(Tmin.seq, mu.ci.CP[2,], lty=2, col="grey60")

Any ideas?

Iara

--

PhD Candidate- UC Davis Ecology Graduate Group

messages.subject: efficient approach to finding consecutive values in a vector?
messages.subject_clean: efficient approach to finding consecutive values in a vector?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm looking for an efficient approach (perhaps one avoiding 'for' loops) to find the position (index) of the 4th "year" position for the first occurrence of 4 consecutive years below a certain value.

For example, given a time series of 16 years of abundance data in the vector 'z' below, the desired result would be 9, the index of the 4th "year" position for the first occurrence of 4 consecutive years < 100 -- this would mark a year of quasi-extinction. I don't have to worry about NA or other missing data issues.

z <- c(150, 150, 99, 99, 150, 99, 99, 99, 99, 150, 150, 99, 99, 99, 99, 100)

 Also, I've got an approach that works with for loops, but is ridiculously slow when I have to apply it to a large number of vectors. I'm happy to clarify if needed or share the slow code.

Many thanks in advance,
Patrick

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: efficient approach to finding consecutive values in a vector?
messages.subject_clean: [D-RUG]: efficient approach to finding consecutive values in a vector?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Patrick,

I would look into Rle(). It's pretty fast and useful for these types of tasks. For example:

> z < 100
 [1] FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE  TRUE
[13]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE
> rle(z < 100)
Run Length Encoding
  lengths: int [1:7] 2 2 1 4 2 4 1
  values : logi [1:7] FALSE TRUE FALSE TRUE FALSE TRUE ...

You can access the length and value vectors with $lengths and $values. So maybe something like (I have't extensively checked this, be warned):

> rep(rle(z < 100)$lengths == 4, rle(z)$lengths)
 [1] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE  TRUE
[13]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE

and

> which(rep(rle(z < 100)$lengths == 4, rle(z)$lengths))
[1]  6  7  8  9 12 13 14 15

> min(which(rep(rle(z < 100)$lengths == 4, rle(z)$lengths)))
[1] 6

But again — quick solution, haven't checked this extensively. Also, wouldn't the desired result be 6? Did I misunderstand the problem?

V

messages.subject_clean: [D-RUG]: efficient approach to finding consecutive values in a vector?
messages.body_plain:
Hey Patrick,

The code below should be faster, not sure if it's fast enough for your needs.

z <- c(150, 150, 99, 99, 150, 99, 99, 99, 99, 150, 150, 99, 99, 99, 99, 100)

i.low <- which(z < 100)
i.last <- i.low[1]
i.4 <- NA

counter <- 1
for( i in i.low[-1]){
  if(counter == 4) {
    i.4 <- i
    break
  }

  if(i-1 == i.last)
    counter = counter + 1
  i.last <- i
}

messages.subject: adding a vertical line with a different intercept to each facet of a histogram in ggplot2
messages.subject_clean: adding a vertical line with a different intercept to each facet of a histogram in ggplot2
messages.body_plain:
Dear D-RUG folks;

I could use help with a graphic I would like to make.

I made a set of faceted histograms showing the distributions of four groups of observations:

(TST.hist <- ggplot(Hunger, aes(x = TSThrs, group = BedtimeHunger)) + geom_histogram()) + facet_wrap(~ BedtimeHunger, nrow = 4) + theme_bw()

Next, I would like to add a line to each facet showing the mean for that group of observations.  I tried this:

(TST.hist <- ggplot(Hunger, aes(x = TSThrs, group = BedtimeHunger)) + geom_histogram()) + facet_wrap(~ BedtimeHunger, nrow = 4) + theme_bw() + geom_vline(xintercept = mean(Hunger$TSThrs, na.rm = TRUE), col = "red")

But it drew a line at the grand mean, not the mean of each group (as shown in the attachment).

Then I tried this:

(TST.hist <- ggplot(Hunger, aes(x = TSThrs, group = BedtimeHunger)) + geom_histogram() + theme_bw() + geom_vline(data=aggregate(Hunger$TSThrs, list(Hunger$BedtimeHunger), mean, na.rm = TRUE), mapping=aes(xintercept = x), color="red")) + facet_wrap(~ BedtimeHunger, nrow = 4)

But it drew four lines on each facet showing the means of all four groups (as shown in the second attachment).

Does anyone have an idea for how to get one line on each facet showing the mean for that group?

Thanks a bunch for your help!

Bonnie

Bonnie M. Dixon, MCP
Doctoral Candidate in Nutritional Biology

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: adding a vertical line with a different intercept to each facet of a histogram in ggplot2

messages.body_plain:
There's an example of this in the online documentation at http://docs.ggplot2.org/0.9.3.1/geom_vline.html. You need to create a second data.frame holding the means and organized by the facet variable. So, using plyr::ddply:
library(plyr)
TST.hist <- ggplot(Hunger, aes(x = TSThrs, group = BedtimeHunger)) + geom_histogram()) + facet_wrap(~ BedtimeHunger, nrow = 4) + theme_bw()
TST.hist.vlinedata <- ddply(Hunger, "BedtimeHunger", summarize, BedMean=mean(TSThrs))
TST.hist <- TST.hist + geom_vline(aes(xintercept=BedMean),  TST.hist.vlinedata, col="red")
